name: Hexagon
description: Optimal tessellation geometry minimizing perimeter-to-area ratio. Nature's preferred packing solution found in honeycombs, basalt columns, and molecular structures.

core_attributes.pattern: plane tessellation, minimal perimeter, maximum packing

scope.definition: Area coverage fraction achieved by hexagonal close-packing relative to maximum possible 2D area coverage — compared to square (0.785) and random packing (0.64) for equal circles.

evidence.source: Hales (1999) 'The honeycomb conjecture', Discrete and Computational Geometry 25:1-22; Kepler (1611) 'Strena Seu de Nive Sexangula' (on hexagonal snow crystal geometry).
cross_domain_examples: hexagonal packing achieves π/(2√3) = 0.9069 area coverage — mathematically proven maximum for equal circles
honeybee comb uses hexagonal cells: 0.9069 wax area efficiency vs 0.785 for square cells
graphite basal plane: hexagonal carbon bonding achieves maximum electron delocalization per atom
columnar basalt: hexagonal fracture pattern minimizes surface energy during thermal contraction

scope.falsifiability: If any regular polygon tiling of equal-diameter circles achieves coverage above 0.9069, the hexagonal maximum is disproven.
scope.measurement_limits: The 0.9069 applies to perfect hexagonal packing of equal circles. Honeybee cells deviate slightly (cylindrical larvae require rounded corners) — real efficiency is 0.88-0.91.
